messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I can’t compute a slope gradient from just latitude/longitude coordinates.  
A slope (in degrees, percent, or ratio) is defined as the change in elevation divided by the horizontal distance between two points:

\[
\text{slope} = \frac{\Delta \text{elevation}}{\Delta \text{horizontal distance}}
\]

The coordinates you supplied (40.7128 N, –74.0060 W) and (34.0522 N, –118.2437 W) give us the horizontal separation (which we could calculate as a great‑circle distance), but we have no information about the vertical difference (e.g., the elevations of those two locations). Without that elevation data, the slope gradient cannot be determined.

If you can provide the elevations (or any other vertical datum) for each point, I can calculate the slope in degrees, percent, or ratio for you.
